title: Concentration of visits to a set
statement: Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space of size $n$, and let $\lambda$ bound its operator norm on vectors orthogonal to the uniform vector, with $0\leq\lambda\leq1$. Let $B$ be a set of states with $|B|=\beta n$, and let $\delta>0$. For every $k\in\mathbb N$, the probability that the fraction of the $k+1$ visited states lying in $B$ differs from $\beta$ by more than $\delta$ is strictly less than $2\exp\!\left(-\frac{(1-\lambda)\delta^2(k+1)}{60}\right)$.
hypotheses_covered: Each row of A sums to one
B is a subset of the state space
caveat: The definition of lambda is a supremum over unit vectors orthogonal to the uniform vector, which may be empty in a one-state space; the usual operator norm wording may then be misleading.
